= Master Parameter List
:toc:
:toclevels: 2

One row per distinct parameter concept, unioned across James Ball's
list and ours. Entries UDB already defines outright are excluded;
56 of his entries were dropped on that basis.

Entries that only *partially* overlap a UDB parameter are kept, with
the overlap recorded in the UDB column. A partial overlap is a
granularity or aspect mismatch, not coverage.

*126 rows*: 30 on both lists, 8 only ours, 88 only his.

NOTE: The `confidence` column is intentionally empty. It is for
reviewers to fill in, on the scale `high | medium | low`, recording
how strongly they believe the row is a real, certifiable parameter.
Ratings from Allen, Umer and James are all welcome in the same
column; put initials alongside the value if more than one person
rates a row.

CAUTION: The two lists do not have equal standing. Every row of ours
was reviewed individually by Allen Baum and Umer; his are an initial
individual effort, explicitly not Parameter SIG consensus. The
`review_status` column carries this per row.

The table below shows the comparison columns only. The full row is
in `master_list.csv` and `master_list.xlsx` alongside this file,
which additionally carry **every field of James' schema verbatim**
-- `long-name`, `description`, `type`, `width`, `range`, `array`,
`note`, `func-of-field-name`, chapter, section and granularity --
as their own `james_*` columns rather than folded into a derived
value. `james_domain` is the one normalised column, kept for the
like-for-like comparison against `ishaan_domain`.

A cell containing ` | ` means the row cites more than one of his
entries, because some of our parameters are umbrellas over several
of his.

== Rows carrying a defect or an open question

107 of 126 rows carry a note. Sources, criteria flags and defects are in the CSV; the substantive ones are reproduced here.

* `MSIP_UPDATE_MAX_TIME` (P049) -- OUT OF SCOPE under our criteria: platform integration or no architectural units. Kept for the mentor to rule on.  UDB check: A maximum time with no architectural units. Excluded by rule 6 (implementation-defined with no testable units or enumerable options).
* `MSTATUS_TW_TIME_LIMIT` (P053) -- OUT OF SCOPE under our criteria: platform integration or no architectural units. Kept for the mentor to rule on.  UDB check: The WFI bounded time limit. Excluded by INCLUSION_CRITERIA rule 6, which names "bounded time limit" as its literal example of an implementation-defined quantity with no testable units.  Flagged by our INCLUSION_CRITERIA rule 6 on `MSTATUS_TW_TIME_LIMIT`: no testable units / 'misconfigured'.
* `MTIME_TICK_PERIOD` (P058) -- OUT OF SCOPE under our criteria: platform integration or no architectural units. Kept for the mentor to rule on.  UDB check: Excluded by rule 4 (NON_ISA, outside ISA scope); Jordan records platform.clock_frequency and instructions_per_tick as having no UDB parameter either.
* `NMI_ADDR` (P062) -- OUT OF SCOPE under our criteria: platform integration or no architectural units. Kept for the mentor to rule on.  UDB check: NMI vector address. Excluded by rule 4 (NON_ISA, platform rather than ISA), not on testability grounds -- it is observable. Scope question for the mentor.  His `NMI_ADDR` cites impl-def ? with no matching normative rule in the pinned manual, so its spec text could not be checked.
* `PMA_MM_IFETCH` (P066) -- UDB check: UDB has PMA_GRANULARITY only; Jordan records UDB as having no per-region PMA attributes.  DEFECT (his file): cites a tag whose sentence does not describe the parameter -- 'Main memory regions always support read and write' says nothing about instruction fetch.
* `RST_ADDR` (P069) -- OUT OF SCOPE under our criteria: platform integration or no architectural units. Kept for the mentor to rule on.  UDB check: Reset vector address.
